conflicts.scope: Committing application code changes. AGENTS.md line 3 declares scope 'all work in this repository', which includes application code; docs/fast-path.md line 3 declares scope 'application code changes'. Both directives therefore apply whenever application code is changed and committed.

conflicts.explanation: Under the same condition (an application-code change headed for a commit) one directive requires running the full test suite and the other requires skipping all tests. The two actions cannot both be performed. The supplied material states no precedence rule between the root file and the linked document, and AGENTS.md line 6 explicitly directs the agent to read the fast path before changing application code, so the agent cannot avoid encountering both directives.

actions.recommendation: Change only docs/fast-path.md line 4 so that the fast path keeps its prompt-reporting intent but no longer instructs skipping tests, leaving the AGENTS.md test gate untouched. This is the smallest edit that removes the incompatibility while preserving every listed constraint verbatim. If the project owner actually intends the fast path to override the test gate, the correct edit is instead a scoped exception added to AGENTS.md line 5, and the owner should confirm that intent before any patch is applied.

patches.rationale: Resolves C1 by removing the instruction to skip all tests, which is incompatible with the repository-wide commit test gate in AGENTS.md line 5, while keeping the immediate-reporting behavior of the fast path.

edits.replacement: When changing application code, run the full test suite before committing, then report the change immediately.

uncertainties: The supplied material does not state whether AGENTS.md or docs/fast-path.md is intended to take precedence, so the choice to edit the fast-path directive rather than add an exception to the AGENTS.md test gate reflects the conservative option of preserving the test gate, not a stated project rule.
It is not established whether 'report the change immediately' is meant to happen before or after committing; the proposed replacement preserves the reporting step but does not resolve that ordering.
